events.title: US August employment report (NFP)
events.why_it_matters: Last jobs print before the Warsh FOMC; consensus ~+55-58k after July's -23k and soft ADP +38k.
events.what_to_watch: Whether payrolls rebound enough to justify a hike or stay weak enough to force a hold.

events.title: FOMC September decision (first Warsh SEP/dots)
events.why_it_matters: Funds rate 3.50-3.75%; Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech and Waller's hold-lean have made this a genuine coin flip (~50-60% hike odds).
events.what_to_watch: NFP today and CPI Sep 11 will gate the decision; SEP dots and Warsh's presser set the path.

events.title: US-Iran Strait of Hormuz conflict escalation
events.why_it_matters: Renewed US-Iran strikes Aug 31 pushed Brent to ~$95 with Hormuz throughput at ~4.9M b/d vs 21.6M pre-war, feeding global inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the ceasefire/MOU framework holds or further strikes hit tanker traffic; OPEC+ spare capacity response.

events.title: US August CPI
events.why_it_matters: July CPI was +3.4% y/y; August will capture late-July/August Hormuz oil spike feeding the energy channel into the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Core m/m and whether energy pass-through is broadening beyond fuel into goods/services.

events.title: US August PPI
events.why_it_matters: July PPI was +4.7% y/y; pipeline read into CPI and the FOMC decision.
events.what_to_watch: Whether producer prices accelerate on oil pass-through ahead of CPI the next day.

events.title: ECB rate decision (Berlin)
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate 2.25%; euro-area flash CPI hit 3.3% y/y in August on energy (+14.3%), markets price ~80-95% odds of a 25bp hike to 2.50%.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Lagarde signals one-and-done or a further tightening path given gas price risks.

events.title: Bank of Japan policy meeting
events.why_it_matters: Policy rate 1.0%; Ueda signaled a hike is on the table this month as yen weakness and energy import costs lift upside inflation risks.
events.what_to_watch: Whether BOJ hikes to 1.25% and yen intervention continues after record $96.5B spent in past month.

events.title: Bank of England rate decision
events.why_it_matters: Bank Rate 3.75% after June/July holds; energy volatility has trimmed hike odds versus the ECB's near-certain move.
events.what_to_watch: MPC vote split and any signal on whether UK inflation is re-accelerating on energy.

events.title: Canada dollar-for-dollar tariffs take effect
events.why_it_matters: Ottawa matches US 50% Section 338 duties on ~$27.6B of US goods (steel, furniture, apparel, dairy, electronics) from 12:01 a.m. Sep 8.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the two sides de-escalate before the deadline or the trade war deepens into the midterms.

events.title: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' iPhone 18 event
events.why_it_matters: First hardware event under CEO John Ternus; expected iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and rumored first foldable (iPhone Ultra).
events.what_to_watch: Pricing, foldable specs, and whether Apple confirms Chinese memory (CXMT) testing amid DRAM supply squeeze.

events.title: Oracle Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Cloud-infrastructure print tests AI-capex spend beyond Nvidia/Dell/Broadcom hardware; consensus ~$19.13B revenue, $1.30 EPS.
events.what_to_watch: OCI backlog, AI cloud growth rate, and margin trajectory after a wild year riding the AI wave.

events.title: Adobe Q3 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Software/AI-tools bellwether tests whether generative-AI monetization is offsetting creative-cloud saturation.
events.what_to_watch: Citi anticipates a 'beat and raise'; watch AI revenue disclosures and guidance.

events.title: OPEC+ core-group meeting (October quotas)
events.why_it_matters: Sources expect unchanged October policy after a ~188kbd September quota step; Hormuz disruptions, not quotas, are the binding supply constraint.
events.what_to_watch: Whether OPEC+ signals a pause given Hormuz chaos and whether Saudi/Russia can offset Iranian losses.

events.title: China August trade data
events.why_it_matters: July exports were +23.9% y/y; August will show whether AI/electronics demand and tariff diversion still offset weak domestic demand.
events.what_to_watch: Chip export strength and whether tariff front-running distorts the numbers.

events.title: China August CPI/PPI
events.why_it_matters: July CPI was only +0.5% y/y; a still-soft print keeps the easing-bias case alive even as PBoC holds LPR at record lows.
events.what_to_watch: Whether PPI stays positive (~+3.5% y/y) on commodity pass-through or deflation pressure returns.

events.title: US August retail sales
events.why_it_matters: July retail sales fell -0.6% (first decline in 9 months); drops on FOMC day two and is the consumer-resilience check.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the consumer is cracking under high gas prices and sticky inflation.

events.title: US Section 232 drone/UAS tariffs live
events.why_it_matters: 100% duties on larger/thermal UAS and 25% on smaller drones went live Sept 3, aimed at China supply chains with 10-15% allied caps.
events.what_to_watch: Compliance costs, allied exemptions, and whether China retaliates on US drone components.

events.title: ISM Services PMI (August) — 55.4 beat
events.why_it_matters: Services PMI surged to 55.4 from 54.1, beating forecasts, but employment sub-index stayed in contraction at 47.8.
events.what_to_watch: Mixed signal: strong demand vs weak hiring complicates the Fed's hike-vs-hold calculus.

events.title: Initial jobless claims — 206k
events.why_it_matters: Claims ticked up to 206k from 204k, still historically low — labor market stable ahead of NFP.
events.what_to_watch: Four-week moving average trend into the September FOMC.

events.title: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 earnings — AI beat but stock slid
events.why_it_matters: Q3 revenue jumped 86% to $29.6B with AI chip sales tripling; but stock fell as Q4 AI guidance ($21.7B) underwhelmed vs aggressive expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the AI-capex trade is becoming 'sell the news' after Nvidia/Dell/Broadcom all confirmed but stocks stalled.

events.title: Google ad tech antitrust ruling — no breakup
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected DOJ bid to force sale of Google's AdX exchange, accepting behavioral remedies instead — third straight Big Tech breakup loss for US enforcers.
events.what_to_watch: Detailed ruling due in 14 days; DOJ appeal prospects and implications for Apple/Epic and other pending antitrust cases.

FOMC September hike risk (coin flip) with Warsh's hawkish bias and sticky inflation

Oracle earnings as AI-cloud demand test with potential upside surprise
US dollar strength on Fed hike odds vs yen intervention limits
summary: Global markets face a high-stakes September with the FOMC decision (Sep 15-16) as the centerpiece, now a genuine coin flip between a hold and a hike under new Chair Warsh. The US-Iran conflict continues to disrupt Hormuz oil flows, pushing Brent to ~$95 and complicating the inflation picture ahead of CPI (Sep 11). Today's NFP report is the key near-term catalyst. Central banks globally (ECB, BOJ, BOE) are all leaning hawkish on energy-driven inflation. Trade tensions are escalating with Canada's retaliatory tariffs due Sep 8 and new chip tariffs announced. The AI trade is showing signs of fatigue after Broadcom's beat-and-slide, while Google's antitrust win provides a rare positive for Big Tech. Apple's iPhone 18 event and Oracle/Adobe earnings offer sector-specific catalysts next week.
